title: Lambda in a VPC (ENIs, endpoints, cold start)
hook: Lambda functions in a VPC get Elastic Network Interfaces in your subnets to reach private resources like RDS — but AWS API calls need NAT Gateway or VPC endpoints.

blocks.text: Configure Lambda with subnet IDs and security group IDs to attach Hyperplane ENIs in your Virtual Private Cloud (VPC). The function can then reach private IP resources such as Amazon RDS or ElastiCache. Without NAT Gateway or interface/gateway VPC endpoints, calls to public AWS APIs (S3, DynamoDB) fail or need endpoints. Subnet IP capacity must cover peak concurrent ENIs.

entries.plainDefinition: Shared network infrastructure for Lambda VPC connectivity.

blocks.text: Classic interview trap: Lambda in private subnet cannot reach S3 — add gateway endpoint or NAT. /28 subnet exhausts under burst concurrency. Split architecture: VPC functions for DB, non-VPC for S3/API.

blocks.title: Interview framing
blocks.body: Say: VPC Lambda for private RDS only. S3 gateway endpoint free. Size subnets for concurrency. Hyperplane reduced ENI cold start vs old model.

sections.heading: How it works step by step

items.title: Pick subnets
items.body: Private subnets in multiple AZs with enough free IPs for peak concurrency.

items.title: Security groups
items.body: Lambda SG egress to RDS SG port; endpoint SG allows 443 from Lambda SG.

items.title: Endpoints or NAT
items.body: S3/DynamoDB gateway endpoints; other APIs via interface endpoints or NAT.

items.title: Test path
items.body: RDS connect from Lambda; S3 access via endpoint route table association.

flowchart TB

snippet.label: Lambda VPC config
snippet.code:
VpcLambda:
  Type: AWS::Lambda::Function
  Properties:
    VpcConfig:
      SecurityGroupIds:
        - !Ref LambdaSecurityGroup
      SubnetIds:
        - !Ref PrivateSubnetA
        - !Ref PrivateSubnetB
    Runtime: nodejs20.x
    Handler: index.handler
snippet.explanation: Subnets must be private with route to endpoints or NAT for AWS API access.

snippet.label: S3 gateway endpoint
snippet.code:
S3Endpoint:
  Type: AWS::EC2::VPCEndpoint
  Properties:
    ServiceName: !Sub com.amazonaws.${AWS::Region}.s3
    VpcId: !Ref AppVpc
    RouteTableIds:
      - !Ref PrivateRouteTableA
      - !Ref PrivateRouteTableB
    VpcEndpointType: Gateway
snippet.explanation: Associate gateway endpoint with route tables used by Lambda subnets.

snippet.label: Update function VPC config
snippet.explanation: Change triggers ENI replumb — expect brief connectivity blip.

snippet.label: Check subnet available IPs
snippet.explanation: Plan /24 or larger per AZ for high concurrency VPC Lambda.

blocks.title: Pitfalls to avoid
blocks.body: Lambda in VPC without S3 endpoint or NAT — AccessDenied or timeout to S3. /28 subnet with 100 concurrent Lambda. Same SG for Lambda and RDS without egress rules on RDS SG referencing Lambda SG.

blocks.text: RDS Proxy reduces connection storm from Lambda scale-out. How to prove it in production: Lambda ENI count in subnet via describe-network-interfaces, failed S3 calls in VPC without endpoint, cold InitDuration delta VPC vs non-VPC.

rows: NAT cost and single-AZ risk if one NAT

blocks.title: What gets you rejected in interviews
blocks.body: VPC Lambda without endpoint path to S3 gets rejected. Strong answer: gateway endpoint for S3, interface for DynamoDB, or split functions.

interviewTakeaways: VPC Lambda needs subnets, SGs, and IP capacity for scale.
Use S3 gateway endpoint — free — instead of NAT for S3 access.
Interface endpoints or NAT required for other AWS APIs from private subnet.
60s: VPC for RDS private IP. S3 gateway endpoint. Size subnet IPs. Split non-VPC for public API Lambdas.
Follow-up: how many IPs does Lambda use per concurrency?
commonPitfalls: No NAT/endpoints in private subnet Lambda — weak answer.
Strong answer: S3 gateway endpoint on route table; interface endpoints for other services.
/28 subnet for high concurrency VPC Lambda.
